thread.title: Apple Stock Is Falling on New Report of iPhone Production Cuts

author: Barron's
title: Apple Stock Is Falling on New Report of iPhone Production Cuts
text:
courtesy of Apple Apple stock (ticker: AAPL) is dropping Monday morning after a report that the tech giant told its suppliers to cut iPhone production for all three new models.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the matter , that Apple has cut orders in recent weeks for all three newly released iPhone models. The media outlet also said the smartphone maker told several suppliers in the past week that it cut its production plan for the iPhone XR again after an initial reduction in late October, some of the people said.
Related Reading
https://www.barrons.com/articles/why-apples-stock-slide-could-continue-1542454201 Apple stock was down 2.6% as the market opened on Monday, to about $188.50 per share. Apple didn't immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.
Apple's $749 iPhone XR became available for sale on Oct. 26. The release came after the company put the $999 iPhone XS and the $1,099 iPhone XS Max on the market in September.
https://asset.barrons.com/dj-mg/dice/barrons-staffpicks-2d590600-c862-4394-b9d3-66b48c376d60/inset.json
Apple shares have fallen more than 11% this month as investors grow increasingly worried about iPhone sales given warnings from suppliers and negative commentary by analysts.
Last week, wireless chip maker Qorvo ( QRVO ) reduced its financial guidance for its third quarter, citing weaker demand for high-end smartphones. And iPhone suppliers Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ) and Japan Display (6740.Japan) lowered their financial forecasts on Nov. 12, prompting a selloff in the stocks of Apple and its suppliers.
Earlier this month, the Nikkei Asian Review also reported the tech giant told its suppliers to cancel plans for additional iPhone XR production lines.
